title: Having Drive
note: He defines ஊக்கம் as being roused to act without the mind weakening. Whoever learns through spies what has happened must act on it and needs drive to do so, so this follows the chapter on spies.

couplets.plain: Drive is what truly counts as having. Do those without it really have whatever else they have?
couplets.pm: What most deserves the word “having” is drive. Those who lack it can’t be said to have even the other things they own. They have no power to keep them, so they will lose them too.

links.quote: Drive is what truly counts as having
links.reason: Lets drive alone earn the name of having, and doubts all other ownership.

links.quote: really have whatever else they have
links.reason: Moves the title of possession from goods to a person’s own drive.

couplets.plain: To have spirit is to truly have something. Having wealth doesn’t last. It slips away.
couplets.pm: Having drive is the possession that stays with you. Having wealth won’t stay, but goes. Drive is a quality of the mind, so it lasts. Wealth is separate from the body and given to perishing, so it doesn’t, and it isn’t truly a possession at all.

links.quote: To have spirit is to truly have something

couplets.plain: Those who hold lasting drive in their hand don’t fret, saying “Our prosperity is lost.”
couplets.pm: Even when it is gone, those who hold lasting drive as their wealth in hand don’t fret, saying “We have lost our wealth.” He gives the reason in the next couplet.

links.quote: hold lasting drive in their hand
links.reason: Drive is the wealth in hand that keeps people from crying that all is lost.

couplets.plain: Prosperity asks the way and goes by itself to someone whose drive never wavers.
couplets.pm: Wealth itself goes, asking the way like a traveller, to the one whose drive doesn’t weaken in hardship. So drive, which causes wealth, is greater than any wealth already gained.

links.reason: Credits unwavering drive with drawing prosperity to itself.

links.remove: The Tamil has prosperity asking the way, not a goddess. Neither ஆக்கம் nor his gloss, which says wealth, points to Lakshmi.

couplets.plain: The stem of a water flower is as long as the water is deep. People rise as high as their spirit.
couplets.pm: The stems of water flowers are as long as the standing water is deep. In the same way, people’s height is as great as their drive. As the stem lengthens with the water, people rise as their drive grows. Rising here means growing in wealth and armies.

links.quote: People rise as high as their spirit
The stem of a water flower is as long as the water is deep
links.reason: The depth of the water sets how long a flower’s stem grows, as spirit sets how high people rise.

couplets.plain: Let all your thoughts be of rising higher. Even when it fails, it has the nature of not failing.
couplets.pm: Rulers should think of nothing but their own rising. Even if fate keeps it from coming about, that aim has the nature of not failing. Mostly it doesn’t fail, and when it does there has been no lapse in effort, so good people don’t blame them.

links.quote: Let all your thoughts be of rising higher
links.reason: Urges every thought towards rising, for such an aim does not fail even when it fails.

links.quote: Even when it fails, it has the nature of not failing
links.reason: Tells one who fell short that a high aim has the nature of not failing.

couplets.plain: The strong don’t falter when things fall apart. An elephant struck by a mass of arrows stands its ground.
couplets.pm: An elephant wounded by a sheaf of arrows doesn’t weaken, but holds to its greatness. In the same way, those with drive don’t weaken when the rising they aimed at meets ruin, but hold to their greatness. Even if it fails, they go on and finish what they set out to do.

links.quote: The strong don’t falter when things fall apart
links.reason: Says those with drive do not falter even when things fall apart.

links.quote: An elephant struck by a mass of arrows stands its ground
links.reason: The struck elephant stands its ground instead of giving way.
The mass of arrows is the blow of ruin, and it doesn’t bring the strong down.

links.quote: don’t falter when things fall apart
links.reason: Offers someone whose plans have fallen apart a picture of standing firm under the wound.

couplets.plain: Those without spirit will never have the pride of thinking, “In this world, we are the generous ones.”
couplets.pm: Rulers without drive never reach the pride of rating themselves generous among the people of this world. Without drive there is no effort, without effort no wealth, without wealth no giving, and without giving no pride. The joy of winning through giving is known only to the giver, so he puts it in the first person.

links.quote: Those without spirit will never have the pride
links.reason: Shows what lack of spirit costs: the pride of being generous.

couplets.plain: An elephant may be huge and sharp of tusk, yet it fears a tiger’s attack.
couplets.pm: The elephant has the largest body of all beasts and sharp tusks as well, yet it fears the tiger it meets. It has more strength and better weapons, but no drive, and the tiger has drive. This is said of something else: rulers stronger and better armed than their enemies, if they have no drive, fear enemies who have it.

links.quote: huge and sharp of tusk, yet it fears

links.reason: The giant’s fear before the tiger shows size without spirit.

couplets.plain: A person’s strength is wealth of spirit. Those without it are trees. Only their human shape sets them apart.
couplets.pm: A person’s firm understanding is abundance of drive. Those without it aren’t people but trees, differing only in human shape. They lack the good sense and effort of people, so they are trees. They lack a tree’s use too, its fruit and its timber for temples, houses, chariots and ships, so they differ from trees.
couplets.note: He takes உரம், strength, as firm understanding.
couplets.sensitive: calls people without drive lifeless wood

links.quote: A person’s strength is wealth of spirit

links.reason: People without spirit are trees in human shape.

ideaLinks.quote: Those without spirit will never have the pride of thinking
ideaLinks.reason: Without spirit behind it, the pride of being generous can’t be had.
